newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Australia says commitment to Asia top priority.
newsitem.headline: Australia says commitment to Asia top priority.

text.p: Australia's top priority remains the expansion of links with Asia and the current race row should not deter Asian tourists from visiting the country, the country's deputy prime minister said on Saturday.
Tim Fischer, who is also minister for trade, told reporters that Asia was not Australia's only priority, but it was its top priority.
"This view is not only held by the government, and to be fair the opposition, but by federal and state parliaments in Australia generally," he said.
A row over race began in September when independent politician Pauline Hanson made her maiden parliamentary speech, in which she said Austrlia risked being swamped by Asians.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard initially kept silent about the speech. When pushed to condemn it, he complained Hanson was getting too much attention from the press.
Asian media have given widespread coverage to the row, which has led to some Asian tourists -- including a 160-strong group from Singapore -- to cancel trips to Australia.

Asked by Reuters what his message would be to that group of tourists, Fischer replied: "I would appeal to tourists from the Asian area to come on down and visit Australia -- to proceed with their plans.
"There may well have been an over-reaction in some elements of the tourist industry. We are open for tourist business.
"Australia is very much a racially tolerant country. It is able to be judged in that regard very satisfactorily," he said.
Fischer also noted that on Friday, both houses of the Australian parliament had unanimously supported a parliamentary motion against racial intolerance.
Fischer stopped off in Singapore en route to Thailand and India.
